## Key claims (as stated in source)
- The **AI Compute Faculty Development Initiative** is a capacity-building programme to strengthen AI teaching, research, and innovation across Africa.
- **Jointly implemented by AU–ASRIC, the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI), and Peking University**, following the 1st Cohort in April 2026.
- The **1st Cohort attracted over 130 applications from 24 African countries**; participants received intensive training in AI systems, computing infrastructure, and teaching methodologies.
- The **2nd Cohort will select 15 university lecturers** as "Seed Teachers" to replicate AI knowledge, develop curricula, and strengthen institutional AI programmes.
- Training areas: AI systems and computing architecture (CPU/GPU/NPU), ML systems and deep learning execution, AI compilers/optimization, large-scale model training and parallel computing, open-source AI frameworks (e.g., FlagOS ecosystem), curriculum development.
- Eligibility: university lecturer in CS/AI/related field, PhD or equivalent, age ≤45, English or French proficiency.
- Timeline: application deadline June 25, 2026; selection July 30, 2026; programme commencement September 10, 2026.
- 10 universities that benefited from the 1st Cohort are listed (Tunisia, Cameroon, Morocco, Ethiopia, Malawi, Senegal, Ghana, Egypt, Tanzania, South Africa).

## Verification notes
